elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9(h): "Customer may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets ... or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction".

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same carve-out expressly covers a "purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets related to the subject matter" and "any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction", all without approval or consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The opening prohibition ("Neither Party may assign ... without the other Party's prior written consent") is retained and the no-consent proviso is now limited to Customer, so Kubient's assignments — including to its own affiliates or acquirers — are consent-gated.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Existing language retained verbatim: "without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Kubient may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Customer" — an unconditional bar, not merely a consent condition.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Customer's change of control shall not give Kubient any right to terminate this Agreement." No other clause conditions termination on a change of control; the 4(a) post-Initial-Term 90-day right is a separate convenience mechanic not triggered by change of control.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The revised proviso confines the no-consent transfer right to Customer; Kubient has no successor-assignment right, so the mutual formulation of the fallback is not delivered.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears anywhere in rendered 9(h); Customer's carve-out operates "without approval or consent" with no written-notice trigger.

A no-consent non-successor exception is retained — Customer may still assign "to any affiliate" without consent — which under the ASSIGN fallback boundary defeats the requirement that all non-successor assignments be consent-gated.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld", applying mutually to all consent-gated assignments.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment.

The fallback is not met (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and a retained Customer affiliate no-consent exception), but that is immaterial because the higher preferred checklist is fully satisfied.

Minimality holds: the edit changes only "either Party"/"said Party's" to "Customer" in the existing proviso (necessary to gate Vendor assignments) and appends two short clauses tied directly to the competitor-bar and change-of-control elements. The mutual prohibition, the reasonable-consent standard, the void-assignment sentence, the successors-and-assigns sentence and the entire-agreement text are all retained verbatim; no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements are added.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references or contradictory retained sentences. The 4(a) termination and fee mechanics are untouched, and the new change-of-control sentence does not conflict with the post-Initial-Term 90-day convenience right, which is not change-of-control triggered.

"Deviation" is the correct finding status: as drafted, paragraph 9(h) extended the no-consent carve-out to Kubient, permitting transfer of the Agreement to any Kubient affiliate or acquirer — potentially an AP competitor — without our consent, which fails the fallback on a material term.
